macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street slides ahead of Nvidia earnings
items.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply as investors reduced exposure to technology and AI shares before Nvidia’s earnings report. The Dow dropped about 1.6%, the S&P 500 1.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite 1.1%, extending multi-session declines.[1][6]

items.title: Markets increase bets on a December Fed rate hike
items.summary: Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and persistent inflation concerns pushed markets to price a roughly 95% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the December meeting.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. data presents mixed economic signals
items.summary: Retail sales showed resilient consumer demand, while industrial production weakened and import prices rose, with higher petroleum costs contributing to inflation pressure.[1]

items.title: Anthropic maintains proposed IPO price range
items.summary: Anthropic kept its proposed initial public offering range at $70 to $78 per share, making the listing another major test of investor appetite for AI-related companies.[2]

items.title: Disney reports stronger-than-expected results
items.summary: Walt Disney reported sales and earnings above analyst expectations, supported especially by performance in its streaming television business.[3]

items.title: Oil prices rise amid Strait of Hormuz concerns
items.summary: Crude prices advanced as reports indicated that tankers may have struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to inflation and geopolitical concerns.[4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Backpack receives CFTC approval for U.S. crypto derivatives exchange
items.summary: The CFTC approved Backpack Exchange as a designated contract market and Backpack Clearing as a derivatives clearing organization, enabling plans for regulated crypto perpetuals and other derivatives. Backpack’s BP token rose more than 20% after the announcement, with one snapshot showing a 26.64% 24-hour gain.[3][9]

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $65,000 as crypto market remains range-bound
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $64,947, within a roughly $63,336–$65,447 daily range, while Ethereum traded around $1,825. Broader market capitalization remained near $2.2 trillion, with Internet Computer, Basic Attention Token and Hyperliquid among notable gainers.[6][8]

items.title: Injective rises about 11.5% on upgrade and regulatory developments
items.summary: Injective gained approximately 11.45% after launching governance voting for the Veyra mainnet upgrade, scheduled for November 24, and announcing that an affiliate had registered as a U.S. SEC transfer agent. The upgrade is intended to add infrastructure for real-world assets and a new quoting system.[5]

items.title: Zcash climbs more than 10% amid development-fund vote
items.summary: Zcash rose as high as $951.87, up 10.44% over 24 hours, amid a community vote proposing changes to the development fund. The proposal would direct 8% of newly issued ZEC to a new fund and require the removal of 50,000 ZEC from circulation if approved.[10]

items.title: Hong Kong, Swift and banks test tokenized-deposit cross-border payments
items.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Swift, HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China are testing blockchain-based cross-border payments using tokenized deposits. Separately, JPMorgan and Singapore’s DBS connected their blockchain deposit networks for round-the-clock transfers of tokenized U.S. dollars.[2][6]

items.title: Senate procedural vote stalls federal Ethereum-market rules
items.summary: A measure aimed at establishing federal rules for Ethereum markets failed to clear a Senate procedural threshold, preventing it from advancing to full consideration.[1]

items.title: Trezor reports logistics-partner data breach
items.summary: Hardware-wallet maker Trezor disclosed that a breach at logistics partner Skladon exposed personal information connected to approximately 27,000 orders. The report did not indicate that wallet private keys were compromised.[8]

items.title: Aster investigates alleged $4.56 million unauthorized transfer
items.summary: A user alleged that an exposed proxy key on decentralized perpetuals platform Aster enabled an abnormal transfer totaling $4.56 million. Aster said it formed an investigation team.[8]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Microsoft unveils seven AI models targeting coding, cybersecurity and enterprise workloads
items.summary: Microsoft announced seven MAI models at its Ignite conference, spanning coding, cybersecurity, image editing, speech, transcription and automated decision-making. The company says the models deliver competitive performance at substantially lower cost than leading OpenAI and Anthropic systems.[1][2]

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra for complex professional and scientific work alongside GPT-6.2 Sol, a more general-purpose and lower-cost model. Both are available through ChatGPT Work, Codex and the OpenAI API, with Astra featuring updated safeguards and improved efficiency.[5][10]

items.title: AlphaGenome sequel improves prediction of disease-linked DNA variation
items.summary: A new version of AlphaGenome can predict how small DNA-sequence changes affect gene activity across multiple cell types, potentially improving understanding of genetic disease mechanisms.[6]

items.title: Microsoft makes Decision 1.1 generally available
items.summary: Microsoft released Decision 1.1 for fast, low-cost classification, prioritization and business workflow decisions. The model is available through Microsoft Foundry and platforms including OpenRouter and Vercel.[8]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches this week
items.summary: Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled for release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, returning players to a modernized Vice City after a 13-year wait. A PC version is expected later.

items.title: BARKOUR release postponed
items.summary: Varsav Game Studios postponed BARKOUR’s planned fourth-quarter 2026 launch on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, citing additional development and testing work after expanding the game’s scope.

items.title: Madden NFL 27 adds Madden ’97 throwback content
items.summary: An upcoming Madden NFL 27 update adds the 1997 All Madden Team, featuring players including Steve Young, Emmitt Smith and Deion Sanders, to Play Now mode on current platforms.

items.title: Take-Two restructures Firaxis
items.summary: Take-Two is reducing staff at Firaxis, the studio behind Civilization and XCOM, as it refocuses on strategy-game design, technology and player experience.

items.title: The Game Awards 2026 nominees announced
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI was included among the nominees for Game of the Year despite not yet being released. Other listed contenders include 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

items.title: New games release ahead of GTA VI
items.summary: Disney Dreamlight Valley: The Keepsake Sea and Goat Simulator 3: Ticket to Dizzyworld are among the games scheduled to release on November 18, with GTA VI following on November 19.
